CANNON-RECOIL-STARBOARD — Braced wide-legged at the starboard gun-deck, his shoulder slammed against the brass breech as the sky-cannon kicks backward mid-fire, smoke erupting from the muzzle in a billowing grey wall, a spent shell spinning past his boot, coat-tails whipping in the recoil-blast, the enemy frigate's hull filling the smoke beyond — the next round is already in his hand.

BOARDING-LEAP — Launching from the gunwale mid-dogfight, both ships barely ten feet apart, a brass pistol extended in his right hand and a cutlass trailing in his left, coat streaming horizontal, cannon-flash from below lighting his face copper, the enemy deck rushing up to meet his boots in the next heartbeat.

CUTLASS-PARRY-GUNWALE — Twisted hard at the waist on the port-side gunwale, both arms raised to catch a sky-cutlass blow, sparks cascading where the blades grind together, his free hand white-knuckled on the brass railing, an enemy boarder already pivoting for a second swing, the open sky wheeling behind them both.

SPEAKING-TUBE-COMMAND — Bent over the chart-table on the bridge with his lips pressed to a brass speaking-tube, one fist driving a divider point into the course-line, amber gauge-light rippling across his face, the ship shuddering under him from a cannon-hit — his next exhaled word will change the heading by forty degrees.

SPYGLASS-HELM — Gripping the ship's wheel with his left hand, body canted forward into the slipstream, a brass spyglass raised to his eye with his right, coat snapping hard against his arm, the horizon alive with enemy signal-smoke — in one second he will spin the wheel hard to starboard.

RIGGING-STORM-REPAIR — Halfway up the portside rigging in driving rain, knees hooked over a ratline, a brass wrench clenched between his teeth, gauntleted hands yanking a torn fin-brace back into its housing, lightning forking white across the dirigible-spine directly behind him — the brace will either seat or snap in the next pull.

SWINGING-RIGGING-LEAP — Mid-swing on a hawser-line between the two locked ships, body fully suspended above the gap, a cutlass raised in his free hand, both vessels' gun-smoke rising around him, rope burning through his gauntlet, coat billowing open — his boots will slam the enemy crow's nest platform in under a second.

SIGNAL-FLARE-GUNWALE — Standing at the port-rail with his arm thrown fully overhead, a brass-handled flare pistol just fired, the red-smoke corkscrew still tight and climbing, the muzzle-bloom fading orange against his face, coat snapping sideways in the altitude-wind — his eyes are already tracking whether the allied ship has seen the signal.

VORTEX-PROW-STAND — Planted feet-wide on the bowsprit platform as the airship noses into a vortex-spiral, coat streaming straight back in a rigid banner, both hands locked on the prow-rail's brass stanchions, cloud-wall spinning ahead in a grey-green churn — the ship's nose will plunge another thirty degrees in the next second.

ASTROLABE-CLOUD-DECK — Leaning back against the observation-railing on the navigation-deck, astrolabe held at arm's length toward a break in the overcast, fingers adjusting the alidade ring, the reading-lamp behind him swinging on its gimbal in the turbulence, coat pressed flat against his ribs by the upwelling wind — the fix will either confirm or contradict the dead-reckoning.

ENGINE-VALVE-CRISIS — Torso wedged into the engine-room housing between two brass manifolds, both hands wrapped around a misfiring pressure-valve, steam jetting white past his ear, sweat and condensation streaking his face, the deck vibrating with a terminal shudder — one more quarter-turn and the valve either seals or bursts.

PISTOL-FIRE-BOARDER — Body twisted mid-step on the gun-deck gangway, a brass pistol discharged point-blank at a boarder mid-leap from the rail, muzzle-flash blooming between them, smoke obscuring the boarder's face, his own arm recoiling back toward his shoulder — he is already reaching for the second pistol at his hip.

SPOTTER-PLATFORM-SWEEP — Leaning far out from the spotter-platform high in the upper rigging, one arm hooked through the brass safety-bar, a spyglass extended into the slipstream, coat-tails fully horizontal and snapping, the main-deck a toy-size rectangle far below — his grip will tighten as the enemy formation comes into focus.

HAWSER-HAUL-LISTING — Thrown back against the severe cant of the listing deck, hauling hand-over-hand on a braided hawser rigged to the counterweight-spar, boots scrabbling on oil-dark planking, rain sheeting horizontal past his silhouette, every tendon in his neck taut — the ship will either answer the pull or roll another five degrees.

CANNON-FUSE-LIGHTING — Crouched low beside the forward cannon on the gun-deck, a brass match-striker sparking in his cupped hands, the cannon's fuse-port open and waiting, an enemy hull enormous in the gun-port beyond, his coat pooled behind him in the crouch — in two seconds the gun will fire and the recoil will throw him aside.

SPAR-SPRINT-CUTLASS — Running the full length of the upper spar above the envelope, arms out for balance, a cutlass raised in his right hand, an enemy grapple-crew scrambling toward him from the far end, wind tearing at his coat, the ground-level sky vertigo-far below — the gap between them will close in four running strides.

SIGNAL-LANTERN-COMMAND — Hanging one-handed off the signal-bracket on the bridge-wing, brass signal-lantern swinging in the other hand, his body cantilevered out over the open air to catch the sightline of the allied ship ahead, coat billowing open, the lantern's shutter clacking through a coded sequence — the reply flash has just appeared on the distant hull.

CLOCKWORK-BIRD-RELEASE — Braced at the stern-rail in the slipstream, both hands opening to launch a clockwork messenger-bird, its brass wings already blurring to speed, a scroll-canister glinting at its belly, his coat shoved back from the wing-downwash — he is already looking toward the target ship to watch for its arrival.

DIVING-PROW-CLING — Flattened against the prow-housing as the airship noses into a steep dive, arms locked around the brass figurehead-brace, feet lifted off the deck by the acceleration, coat pressed flat to his back then flaring at the hem, the cloud-cover rushing upward past him — the next second will either level the dive or steepen it.

CHART-BRASS-QUILL — Bent hard over the navigation-table in the chart-room below the bridge, a brass-tipped quill dragging a new course-line across the vellum chart, his other hand holding down the curling edge, gas-lit gauges glowing amber in a row behind him, the ship yawing slightly under a wind-shear — the line will reach the new waypoint marker in one more stroke.

ENEMY-DECK-LANDING — One boot already on the enemy gunwale, the other still clearing the gap, body low and forward, a cutlass sweeping wide for balance and threat, cannon-smoke from the enemy's own guns rolling past him, coat trailing like a flag — the enemy crew in the smoke ahead has just registered his arrival.

SPEAKING-TUBE-BROADSIDE — Gripping the helm-rail with one fist, the other arm fully extended with a brass speaking-tube pressed to his mouth, mid-shout, the entire ship heeling under a broadside impact, gauge-panels flickering amber to red behind him, his body thrown sideways by the list — the word in the tube is a firing order.

FIN-BRACE-RIGGING-CRISIS — Both feet on a storm-jostled ratline halfway up the starboard-fin mast, one arm hooked over the spar, the other driving a brass coupling-pin into a split fin-brace with the heel of his palm, sparks jumping from the metal-on-metal contact, the dirigible-envelope bulging and thrashing a foot from his shoulder — the pin needs one more strike to seat.

PISTOL-RECOIL-FLARE-RECON — Kneeling on the observation-sponson above the engine-nacelle, one arm braced on the brass housing, a flare-pistol just fired straight up, wrist jolted back by recoil, the green-smoke trail corkscrewing overhead, his eyes already tilted skyward tracking the signal — an allied silhouette has appeared in the cloud-break directly above.

WHEEL-BROADSIDE-HOLD — Both hands locked on the helm-wheel's brass spokes, torso leaning forward into it, coat blasted flat against his back by a near-miss cannon-shock, the wheel fighting him as the rudder bites, gas-lamp behind him swinging violently on its gimbal — the ship's bow is swinging two degrees per second toward the gap in the enemy line.
